correctness.rationale: For any fixed labels a,b and center w, the event that a,b are leaves sharing w is in bijection with uniform trees on n−2 remaining labels. The Prüfer code has n−4 independent symbols in alphabet n−2; leaf count becomes 2+number empty among n−3 designated bins, proving exact PGF and falling moments. For the unweighted n-tree, count distinct symbols after first Prüfer entry, birth probability (n−1−k)/n; for Palm n−2 tree, eligible symbols birth probability (n−3−k)/(n−2). The difference 2(k+1)/(n(n−2))>0 allows monotone same-uniform coupling for n−4 steps and one extra birth in the unweighted process; yields strict Palm first-order dominance, not only increased expectation. Use E[C]=((n−1)/2)(1−2/n)^(n−3) and the two occupancy means to obtain exact covariance; log expansion gives (2−3/e)/(2e²)>0. Independent full Prüfer decoding at n=4,5,6,7 recovered exact finite covariance and means. Infinite claims rest on deletion and coupling, not finite tests.
residual_risks: The result concerns uniform unrooted labeled trees and C-size bias; does not address conditioning merely on C>0, degree-three cherries or binary phylogenetic trees.
Finite n checks are not used for stochastic order at arbitrary n.

value.rationale: Local sibling-leaf motifs are natural measures of symmetry and clustering in Cayley trees; size-biasing by their number is the exact Palm interpretation of sampling a random cherry. The complete finite-n law, stochastic comparison and covariance constant quantify how selecting a local motif changes a global tree statistic. Neither separate marginal means nor the already-known cherry expectation determines these results.
residual_risks: The deletion bijection is short and classic Prüfer occupancy is standard; value rests on full stochastic order and mixed-statistic law, not on routine mean alone.
